slides.title: “I can read it. Can I explain it?”
slides.notes: The persona is an illustrative adult engineering student, not a testimonial. Target situations: study between lectures, distance/off-campus learning, difficulty linking a diagram to physical behaviour, and explaining practical reasoning. Do not claim all students experience this or that KAIRO substitutes for a laboratory.

slides.title: The teaching method has a research basis
slides.notes:
Freeman et al., PNAS 2014, meta-analysis of225 undergraduate STEM studies: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1319030111 . This supports studying active learning, not the claim that KAIRO replicates the reported effect. Karpicke/Roediger2008 retrieval experiment involved vocabulary: https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1152408 . Feedback study https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18605878/ . PhET https://phet.colorado.edu/en/research emphasises iterative learner testing and limits of simulations for physical equipment skills. KAIRO has no measured learning gain; plan equivalent pre/post/delayed transfer with a comparator.
Freeman2014 aggregate exam performance effect was0.47standarddeviations. This is not0.47percentagepoints, not a KAIRO effect and not proof of local transfer. No simulation replaces all physical laboratory skills.
